previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted with shortness of breath, fevers, and dizziness eleven days after discharge to rehab following a fall with rib fractures. Imaging revealed a moderate left pleural effusion, concerning for hemothorax, and a new right lower lobe consolidation suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated for healthcare-associated pneumonia with intravenous vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. A chest tube was placed, draining 1200 cc of serosanguinous fluid, with resolution of the effusion and improvement in respiratory status. He developed dizziness and left-sided coordination issues, but MRI brain showed no acute abnormality; neurology attributed symptoms to neuropathy. His hemoglobin dropped to 6.7 g/dL, prompting a single unit of packed red blood cells. His diabetes was managed with adjustment of Lantus dose to prevent hypoglycemia. He was discharged to the same rehab facility on oral antibiotics, pain control, and instructions for slow mobilization due to neuropathy and fall risk.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with history of multiple myeloma s/p relapse 
after autologous transplant, now on cycle #2 of RVD, who 
presents from ___ clinic with low grade fevers, cough, and 
shortness of breath.

ACUTE ISSUES:
#Fevers, shortness of breath, concern for pulmonary infection:  
Already covered for CAP/HCAP in clinic the day of presentation 
with Levaquin, Vancomycin, Flagyl. Hemodynamically stable, CXR 
WNL. He was continued to be covered for CAP only on the floor, 
as he appeared clinically well. Influenza PCR negative, 
respiratory viral screen and culture returned negative. He was 
empirically given Tamiflu in clinic, which was discontinued upon 
arrival to the floor. He was given Levofloxacin to continue for 
a total ___lthough this was likely a viral 
presentation of URI. He did have significant wheezing in-house, 
which was covered by DuoNebs q6hr, as well as Albuterol and 
Fluticasone inhalers. He was discharged with scripts for both 
Albuterol and Fluticasone. Blood cultures were pending at the 
time of discharge. 

# Multiple myeloma: Patient received an infusion of IVIg during 
this admission on ___, which he tolerated well. He remained 
hemodynamically stable and afebrile throughout the infusion; he 
however was noted to be diaphoretic, which resolved 
post-infusion. Enoxaparin and Lenalidomide were held per his 
primary Oncologist throughout his stay due to his 
thrombocytopenia. No HSQ was administered this admission. 
Patient was continued on his home Acyclovir. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Diabetes: Patient was continued on his home Glargine 25 units 
at bedtime, in addition to a sliding scale. He was maintained on 
a Diabetic/Consistent carbohydrate diet as well. 

# HBV: Patient was continued on his home Lamivudine. 

# Hx of falls: Patient was continued on his home 
Fludrocortisone. 

# Hypertension: Patient's SBP on admission was in the 140s. He 
was continued on his home Amlodipine and Labetalol, and remained 
normotensive throughout his stay.

# Rib pain: Secondary to fractures sustained during a fall. 
Patient was continued on his home Gabapentin as well as 
Oxycontin/Oxycodone regimen. 

# Depression: Patient was continued on his home Duloxetine and 
Methylphenidate. 

# GERD: Patient was continued on his home Omeprazole. 

ONCOLOGIC PLAN: C2D14 of Borrezomib; plan after acute episode 
resolves per primary Oncologist.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
- Patient is to complete a 7-day course of Levofloxacin, with 
the last dose at the end of the day on ___.
- Patient was diaphoretic with IVIg infusion, but never febrile.
